WITH daily AS (
  SELECT service_date, SUM(trips) AS day_trips
  FROM trips_daily
  WHERE service_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND service_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY service_date
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(day_trips), 1) AS avg_trips_per_day
FROM daily;
notes: Assumes "per day" means the average of daily total trips across all providers and boroughs over the dates in 2025 that have data in trips_daily (days with no rows are excluded, not counted as zero).

sql: SELECT strftime(service_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(trips) AS total_trips FROM trips_daily WHERE service_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND service_date < DATE '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY total_trips DESC LIMIT 1;
notes: Assumes trips_daily is the source for trip counts, summed across all provider types and boroughs, and that "2025" means service_date within calendar year 2025.

sql: WITH yearly AS (SELECT EXTRACT(year FROM service_date) AS yr, SUM(trips) AS total_trips FROM trips_daily WHERE EXTRACT(year FROM service_date) IN (2024, 2025) GROUP BY 1) SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN yr = 2024 THEN total_trips END) AS trips_2024, MAX(CASE WHEN yr = 2025 THEN total_trips END) AS trips_2025, ROUND(100.0 * (MAX(CASE WHEN yr = 2025 THEN total_trips END) - MAX(CASE WHEN yr = 2024 THEN total_trips END)) / MAX(CASE WHEN yr = 2024 THEN total_trips END), 1) AS pct_change FROM yearly
notes: Assumes "trips" means the sum of trips in trips_daily for calendar years 2024 and 2025 (all providers and boroughs), with percent change computed as (2025 − 2024) / 2024.

sql: SELECT borough, SUM(total_pickups) AS total_pickups, SUM(ontime_pickups) AS ontime_pickups, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(ontime_pickups) / NULLIF(SUM(total_pickups), 0), 1) AS ontime_pct FROM pickup_otp_daily WHERE service_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND service_date < DATE '2026-01-01' GROUP BY borough ORDER BY ontime_pct ASC NULLS LAST
notes: Assumed on-time % is pooled over all provider types and standards in 2025 (sum of on-time pickups divided by sum of total pickups), and "worst first" means lowest on-time percentage first.

sql:
SELECT
    provider_type,
    SUM(total_pickups) AS total_pickups,
    SUM(ontime_pickups) AS ontime_pickups,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(ontime_pickups) / NULLIF(SUM(total_pickups), 0), 1) AS ontime_pct
FROM pickup_otp_daily
WHERE service_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND service_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  AND LOWER(provider_type) IN ('primary', 'broker')
GROUP BY provider_type
ORDER BY provider_type;
notes: Assumes provider_type values are "Primary" and "Broker" (matched case-insensitively), on-time % is total on-time pickups over total pickups across all standards and boroughs for calendar 2025, and the query is not weighted by daily/borough averages.

sql:
SELECT
  strftime(service_date, '%Y-%m') AS month,
  SUM(total_pickups) AS total_pickups,
  SUM(ontime_pickups) AS ontime_pickups,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(ontime_pickups) / NULLIF(SUM(total_pickups), 0), 1) AS ontime_pct
FROM pickup_otp_daily
WHERE service_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
  AND service_date < DATE '2027-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
notes: Assumes on-time rate is total ontime_pickups divided by total_pickups across all providers, standards, and boroughs, covering 2026 dates through the current date (2026-11-23) with no further filter.

sql:
WITH src AS (
  SELECT CAST(EXTRACT(year FROM service_date) AS INTEGER) AS yr,
         service_date,
         total_pickups,
         ontime_pickups
  FROM pickup_otp_daily
  WHERE standard ILIKE '%30%'
),
full_years AS (
  SELECT yr
  FROM src
  GROUP BY yr
  HAVING MIN(service_date) = make_date(yr, 1, 1)
     AND MAX(service_date) = make_date(yr, 12, 31)
)
SELECT s.yr AS year,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(s.ontime_pickups) / SUM(s.total_pickups), 1) AS ontime_pct
FROM src s
JOIN full_years f USING (yr)
GROUP BY s.yr
ORDER BY ontime_pct DESC
LIMIT 1;
notes: Assumed the 30-minute standard is identified by ILIKE '%30%' on the standard column (exact label not verified), pooled all provider types and boroughs by summing pickups, and limited to calendar years whose data spans Jan 1 through Dec 31 so the partial current year is excluded.

sql:
WITH complaints_2024 AS (
  SELECT SUM(complaints) AS total_complaints
  FROM complaints_daily
  WHERE opened_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND opened_date < DATE '2025-01-01'
),
trips_2024 AS (
  SELECT SUM(trips) AS total_trips
  FROM trips_daily
  WHERE service_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND service_date < DATE '2025-01-01'
)
SELECT
  c.total_complaints AS complaints_2024,
  t.total_trips AS trips_2024,
  ROUND(1000.0 * c.total_complaints / NULLIF(t.total_trips, 0), 1) AS complaints_per_1000_trips
FROM complaints_2024 c
CROSS JOIN trips_2024 t;
notes: Assumes complaints and trips are both comparable across all provider types and boroughs, so I summed each table separately for calendar 2024 and divided, avoiding a join that could double-count.

WITH bounds AS (
  SELECT MIN(service_date) AS lo, MAX(service_date) AS hi FROM trips_daily
),
yearly AS (
  SELECT YEAR(service_date) AS yr, SUM(trips) AS total_trips
  FROM trips_daily
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT y.yr AS year, y.total_trips AS trips
FROM yearly y
CROSS JOIN bounds b
WHERE b.lo <= make_date(y.yr, 1, 1)
  AND b.hi >= make_date(y.yr, 12, 31)
ORDER BY y.total_trips ASC
LIMIT 1;
notes: Assumes "trips" means the total of the trips column in trips_daily across all provider types and boroughs, and "full calendar year" means the data covers January 1 through December 31 of that year, so partial first or last years are excluded.

sql:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT provider_type, SUM(complaints) AS complaints
  FROM complaints_daily
  WHERE opened_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND opened_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY provider_type
),
t AS (
  SELECT provider_type, SUM(trips) AS trips
  FROM trips_daily
  WHERE service_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND service_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY provider_type
),
by_provider AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(c.provider_type, t.provider_type) AS provider,
         c.complaints,
         t.trips
  FROM c FULL OUTER JOIN t ON c.provider_type = t.provider_type
),
overall AS (
  SELECT 'All providers' AS provider,
         SUM(complaints) AS complaints,
         SUM(trips) AS trips
  FROM by_provider
)
SELECT provider,
       complaints,
       trips,
       ROUND(1000.0 * complaints / trips, 1) AS complaints_per_1000_trips
FROM (SELECT * FROM by_provider UNION ALL SELECT * FROM overall)
ORDER BY provider;
notes: Assumes "last year" means calendar 2025 (today is 2026-11-23), complaints and trips are matched by provider_type only since complaints_daily has no borough, and the rate is total complaints divided by total trips times 1,000.

sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(ride_time_min) * 1.0 / SUM(trips), 1) AS avg_ride_time_min FROM ride_time_monthly WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM month) = 2025

WITH ns AS (
  SELECT month, no_shows_per_1000
  FROM provider_no_shows_monthly
  WHERE provider_type = 'Broker' AND YEAR(month) = 2024
),
tr AS (
  SELECT CAST(DATE_TRUNC('month', service_date) AS DATE) AS month, SUM(trips) AS trips
  FROM trips_daily
  WHERE provider_type = 'Broker' AND YEAR(service_date) = 2024
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(ns.no_shows_per_1000 * tr.trips / 1000.0), 0) AS est_broker_no_shows_2024
FROM ns
JOIN tr USING (month);
notes: The no-show table only stores a monthly rate per 1,000 (assumed to be per 1,000 trips), so the count is estimated by multiplying each month's rate by that month's Broker trips from trips_daily and summing; the provider_type value 'Broker' is assumed to match exactly.
